core.title: Flow router routes go through the flow router runner, and every route ends in the user/system flow runner
core.given: The composition root (the journey router) has a journey map that declares at least one flow router route object (a route of the form {flowRouterId, path})
core.when: you write or change the composition root
core.then: The composition root MUST resolve each flow router route through the flow router runner, and the user/system flow runner MUST perform the final user/system flow execution for every route: both the user/system flow the flow router runner selects and each directly named user/system flow id.
prefer: Delegation chain: the composition root asks the flow router runner to resolve the action to a selected user/system flow (with the action's inputs and the current state) and hands the selected user/system flow id to the user/system flow runner for execution
Use the runner API that actually exists in this stack rather than copying a call model or a fix hint verbatim
avoid: Declaring a flow router route without routing it through the flow router runner
Never reaching the user/system flow runner for the flow-router-selected user/system flow
Executing directly named train-id routes through any executor other than the user/system flow runner
unless: The journey map declares no flow router route object: a purely direct-train composition root carries no flow router obligation
core.why: In both cases, direct and flow router, the user/system flow runner performs the final user/system flow execution. A composition root that declares a flow router route but never routes through the flow router runner, or never reaches the user/system flow runner, breaks the contract.
evidence: The stack's check for this obligation reports no finding for the composition root: neither an unlinked flow router route nor missing delegation to the user/system flow runner
The composition root references the flow router runner and the user/system flow runner whenever the journey map holds a flow router route object
Both directly named train-id entries and flow-router-selected user/system flows reach the user/system flow runner for final execution
verification: The check scans the composition root and triggers only when the journey map declares at least one flow router route object; activation depends only on that presence, not on other detector findings, and the check does not fire for a purely direct-train composition root or for files outside the composition root

When triggered, a missing reference to the flow router runner is reported as an unlinked flow router route, and a missing reference to the user/system flow runner as missing delegation; the concrete finding identifiers are the realization's
Which entrypoint is inspected, and how the journey map, its route forms and the runner references are recognized, is up to the per-stack detector

Disposition strict, severity 4: an unlinked or non-delegating composition root cannot be suppressed and fails CI — a failing check run must fail the continuous-integration build, not merely report the finding

The automated check verifies only that the user/system-flow-runner reference is present; that directly named train-id entries are actually executed by the user/system flow runner must be confirmed by reviewing the dispatch

values: the journey map of the composition root contains at least one flow router route object {flowRouterId, path}

fires: A task adds a flow router route object to the composition root's journey map
An agent edits a composition root whose journey map already holds flow router route objects, including its direct-route dispatch
The composition root declares a flow router route but does not reference the flow router runner or the user/system flow runner
doesNotFire: The journey map holds only directly named train-id entries
Files other than the composition root

neutralityNotes: Journey router, journey map, flow router route object {flowRouterId, path}, flow router runner, user/system flow runner and user/system flow id are the ATDD runtime's shared domain vocabulary (the agnostic core obligation coder.user-system-flow.journey-router-flow-router-routing, core runtime spec afokapu/atdd#1251), so they remain in the core; only their concrete identifiers (server.ts, the JOURNEY_MAP export, the FlowRouterRunner/FlowRunner classes and their resolveUserSystemFlow/execute signatures, the ./user-system-flows/* import paths, checks/flow_router_station_routing.mjs, and the finding ids 'unlinked'/'no delegation') are Bun and live in bunOnly. CI failure is treated as stack-neutral enforcement (every stack's convention checks gate its continuous-integration build) and is kept in core:verification; only the shared:policy.strict-disposition cross-reference pointer stays with the realization. Stack scoping (the doesNotFire entry 'Non-Bun stacks' and the atdd.workspace.bun detector-family applicability note) stays with each realization, since a stack-neutral core carries no stack identity. The {flowRouterId, path} route-object shape is kept verbatim as the runtime-level route form shared across stacks; a stack that realizes the route object differently owns its concrete syntax while the core keeps the two-form distinction (directly named user/system flow id vs flow router route object). How the journey map, route forms and runner references are recognized is deliberately deferred to the per-stack detector (core:verification), as the Bun text itself does, so no profile key was proposed for recognition.
